concepts.why: Secular scholar / all: the name is 'The LORD on His throne'; Revelation 4:2 says only 'someone seated on it' and does not name the LORD. Isaiah 6:1, Psalm 99:1 and Isaiah 66:1 already carry the same throne; the Revelation throne can stay under the Throne secondary or be dropped.
Secular scholar: the name says 'everlasting'; Hebrews 12:28 says 'unshakable kingdom', which is not the same word (the other seven say everlasting, eternal, never destroyed, never end).

Secular scholar and Baptist/dispensational reader: the name is Exodus 19:6's words; 1 Peter 2:9 says 'royal priesthood, a holy nation', not 'kingdom of priests', so the name is not what that passage says, and setting it under Exodus 19:6's name asserts the Israel/church identity readers part on. Revelation 1:6 and 5:10 do say 'a kingdom ... priests' and stay.

note_fixes: John 18:37: the verse does not say 'Jews' or 'Israel'; either drop it or extend to John 18:33-37 and give the note 'Are You the King of the Jews?' (18:33)
concepts.why: Secular scholar: the name is 'King of the Jews, King of Israel'; Luke 19:38 says only 'the King who comes in the name of the Lord' (John 12:13 already carries the entry with 'King of Israel'), and John 18:37 says only 'a king'.

concepts.name: Righteousness and justice in the king's reign (plain label)
concepts.why: Secular scholar: 'the foundation of the throne' is said by Psalm 89:14, 97:2 and the Proverbs, but Psalm 72:1-2, Isaiah 11:4-5 and Isaiah 32:1 say no throne and no foundation, so the name says more than three of eight passages. Either a plain label that all eight hold, or drop those three.

concepts.name: The kingdom of God has come upon you
concepts.why: Catholic, Orthodox, Wesleyan and secular scholar: 'in your midst' is the Berean's choice for a disputed word in Luke 17:21 (among / within / in your grasp), so using it in the name takes the side the drafter says is avoided; the original does not settle it. Matthew 12:28 and Luke 11:20 say 'has come upon you' alike. Luke 17:20 stays in 'The kingdom is not ...'.
